body: `apc_store()` returns an array if the input is an array (the 2nd syntax in PHP manual). It seems this is related with your APC because you said it happens to command line only, not Web.
Even if you've installed APC, at command line it's disabled by default. http://php.net/manual/en/apc.configuration.php#ini.apc.enable-cli
So you are trying to say, that a undefined function returns a boolean value? And that would not explain why this starts happening about two weeks ago.
does this error occur when you have apc enabled?

> So you are trying to say, that a undefined function returns a boolean value?

Something like this actually seems to be the case: http://git.php.net/?p=pecl/caching/apc.git;a=blob;f=php_apc.c;h=9615039b396b9e7de983722f523b9eb7b9079322;hb=HEAD#l583

It is not an undefined function, it is not enabled so it returns false.

Same behavior is when apc is not able to allocate memory, so we should add a check for false here.
http://git.php.net/?p=pecl/caching/apc.git;a=blob;f=php_apc.c;h=9615039b396b9e7de983722f523b9eb7b9079322;hb=HEAD#l597

Currently I have no access to the server but i will check in 8 hours. Memory was available (between 2 and 3 GB of free memory and 4GB swap). I will check if `apc.enable_cli` is `on`. Yesterday I saw the modules `apc` and `apcu` enabled via `phpinfo` and via command line via `php -m`.

Ok you are right. I wrote a small test script:

```
<?php

$store = apc_store('apc-test', 'success');

var_dump($store);

$fetch = apc_fetch('apc-test', $ok);

var_dump($fetch);

var_dump($ok);
```

Output on web:

```
bool(true)
string(7) "success"
bool(true)
```

And on command line:

```
bool(false)
bool(false)
NULL
```

I will check my config. I think its to much overhead for every request to check if apc is enabled before activating the cache module, right?
no, we should check for return value being false.
